questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Landing gear must always be completely raised before driving. If it is not fully raised, it can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to open.
The rear trailer to detach from the combination.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency brakes on the trailer will activate.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS helps prevent wheel lockup when braking hard. If ABS detects that wheels are about to lock, it reduces braking pressure to keep wheels rolling.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, you should position the tractor:

options.text: At a 90-degree angle in front of the trailer.
Directly in front of the trailer.
At a 30-degree angle in front of the trailer.
At a 60-degree angle in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up to couple. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and break the landing gear.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:

options.text: A truck driver is driving too fast.
The driver of a vehicle in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
A truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low to the ground and drive slowly through turns and curves.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: Keeping cargo low helps prevent rollovers. Load cargo as close to the ground as possible to keep the vehicle's center of gravity low.

questions.question: Before a trip, you can make sure air flows to all trailers by:

options.text: Checking for moving air inside of each trailer.
Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feeling for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, listen at the rear shut-off valve of the last trailer to check if air is flowing through the entire air brake system. Air escaping from the rear shut-off valves means air is being supplied to all vehicles.

questions.question: In a vehicle equipped with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to a level between:
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: If you must cross traffic while driving a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to cross safely.

questions.question: What does rearward amplification mean?

options.text: Noise that comes from the back of the vehicle.
How many trailers one tractor can pull.

questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the "crack-the-whip" effect. If not handled properly, a trailer can tip over because of rearward amplification.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents.
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all truck driver accident deaths. To prevent a rollover, keep cargo low and centered. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should know that:

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no trailer attached. When driving a bobtail, it takes longer to stop. It will need a longer distance to stop than a tractor pulling a loaded trailer.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: one for service and one for emergencies.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away:

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks out, the trailer will have no working brakes. The wheels will turn freely.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color marks service lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded. Blue marks service lines and red marks emergency lines.

questions.question: When are rollovers most likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Slow down before entering turns and curves, especially with a full load.

questions.question: Trailers built before ____ do not need to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, the driver should:

options.text: Not use the trailer hand brake.
Use the parking brake to straighten the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes to let the wheels grip the road again. Do not use the trailer hand brake because applying brakes is what caused the wheels to lock up.

questions.question: After coupling, there should be ____ between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
